evals.prompt: Here are my CS170 notes on Dijkstra's algorithm: dijkstra_notes.md — turn them into ONE short 3Blue1Brown-style explainer episode (about 2 minutes) with captions.
evals.expected_output: One rendered 480p episode with burned-in captions and an .srt
assertions: Rendered video episode.mp4 exists and is at least 60 seconds long
Subtitles episode.srt exist with at least 10 captions
Final shortest distances stated are correct: S=0, B=1, A=3, C=4, D=7
The agent reviewed rendered frames (contact sheet / frame images saved in outputs)
No overlapping text or content hidden under captions in the final frames (visual check)

evals.prompt: for my deep learning class (CS182) make a 3b1b style video explaining softmax and cross-entropy loss — how logits become probabilities, why we take -log of the correct class's probability, and why the gradient w.r.t. the logits is just p - y. one episode, ~2-3 min, english captions.
evals.expected_output: One rendered 480p episode with burned-in captions and an .srt
assertions: Rendered video episode.mp4 exists and is at least 90 seconds long
Subtitles episode.srt exist with at least 12 captions, in English
Captions explain that the gradient of the loss w.r.t. the logits is p - y
Numbers shown for the worked example are internally consistent (softmax of the logits sums to 1 and matches)
The agent reviewed rendered frames (contact sheet / frame images saved in outputs)
No overlapping text or content hidden under captions in the final frames (visual check)
